articleBody:
Turning a garage into a legal, comfortable living area like a home office, bedroom, or guest suite involves much more than putting up drywall. It is a major transition from an unconditioned utility space to a fully habitable residential room. Use this practical preparation checklist before breaking ground.

- [ ] Check local zoning and parking rules — You need to confirm whether municipal rules allow converting the garage and whether you are required to provide replacement off-street parking.
- [ ] Schedule a structural and slab inspection — Unlevel concrete, missing vapor barriers, or damaged framing must be addressed before turning the floor into living space.
- [ ] Develop scaled architectural floor plans — You must submit accurate drawings detailing proposed walls, doors, windows, lighting, and egress openings to your local building department.
- [ ] Detail your garage door closure design — Replacing the overhead garage door with an exterior wall, entry door, or windows requires proper framing, weatherproofing, and siding tie-ins.
- [ ] Plan code-compliant insulation and ventilation — Habitable living spaces demand specific wall and ceiling insulation values alongside adequate fresh air flow and heating.
- [ ] Map out rough-in plumbing and electrical needs — Adding a bathroom, kitchenette, or heavy utility loads requires pulling proper mechanical and electrical permits early.
- [ ] Verify emergency escape and rescue openings — Bedrooms and living spaces must meet legal egress window sizing and natural lighting standards.
- [ ] Select a licensed, insured general contractor — A written scope specifying who handles permit filings, trade coordination, and municipal sign-offs protects your budget.

How to use this checklist:
Work through these items during the planning phase before purchasing materials or signing construction contracts.
